severity_scale.P0: blocks play or access for a group of players, or breaks multiplayer
severity_scale.P1: significantly degrades the experience for many players

evidence_types.OBSERVED: seen in a run: screenshot, run output or measurement, with a file path

meta.paths: evidence paths are relative to $AUDIT unless they start with a game file name (sabotage-stack.html, shared/, server/), which are relative to $GAME

findings.title: The playfield shrinks to nothing on short or zoomed viewports, and overflows a 1280×800 laptop
findings.what_happens: The stage is sized from viewport height with no minimum. Canvas size measured: 0×1 px at 320×256 (400% zoom, with 341 px of horizontal scroll), 84×122 at 640×400 (200% zoom), 67×97 at 667×375 and 164×238 at 844×390 (phone landscape). At 1280×800 the opposite happens: the canvas runs 25 px past the fold and the Drop button sits at y=839, off screen. Rotating a phone mid-game leaves the canvas below the fold.
findings.repro: Open the game at 1280×800 and zoom the browser to 200% then 400%, or hold a phone in landscape, and press Play solo.
findings.why_it_matters: Low-vision players who zoom get a smaller game, and at 400% no game. Landscape phone players cannot play. Many laptop players see the tower base and the Drop button cut off.
findings.suggested_change: Size the stage as the largest 360:520 box that fits both the available width and height, with a floor of about 240 px wide; below the floor, let the page scroll rather than shrink further. Keep Drop inside the first viewport, and at short heights move the side cards under the stage. The measured sizes are certain; the CSS cause is inferred from behaviour.

findings.title: Forced auto-drop (3.5 s solo, 10 s Teamwork) cannot be adjusted; an untouched solo run is over in 11 seconds
findings.what_happens: In solo a block that waits 3.5 s drops itself wherever it is. With no input the drops came at 3.6, 7.1 and 10.6 s, trimming the block from 200 to 132 to 107 px; the third missed and ended the run before the first vote resolved. There is no setting to lengthen or disable the timer. Reading the vote card for more than 3.5 s has the same effect.
findings.repro: Play solo and do not touch anything.
findings.why_it_matters: Players who need more than 3.5 s to act (switch or dwell input, motor impairment, or simply reading the vote) cannot play. Rated P1 rather than P0 because precise timing is the game's core and remains a barrier with or without this timer; for that group it is nonetheless blocking.
findings.suggested_change: Add a solo assist option: auto-drop off or 10 s, with the run labelled as assisted. Pause the auto-drop clock for the first 2 s of each vote. See F-009 for keeping pressure without clocks.

findings.title: Vote keys 1/2/3 do nothing while the Drop button or the canvas has focus, which is the default
findings.what_happens: Digit keys are ignored whenever the focused element is a button or has role=button. Play solo focuses the Drop button; clicking the stage focuses the canvas (role=button). Measured: focus on Drop + 1 → no vote; canvas + 2 → no vote; Menu + 2 → no vote; nothing focused + 3 or Numpad 1 → vote registered.
findings.repro: Play solo with the keyboard, wait for the vote at 8 s, press 1.
findings.why_it_matters: The advertised way to vote without leaving the drop rhythm fails for keyboard players and for mouse players who clicked the stage. They conclude that voting is broken or do not vote.
findings.suggested_change: Drop the interactive-target guard for digit keys during play; keep only the typing-target guard (inputs, selects). One condition.

findings.title: On phones the vote and effect cards are below the fold, and the play card blocks scrolling to them
findings.what_happens: At 390×844 the vote card starts at y=784 and the effect card at y=1335; at 360×640, y=594 and y=1145. When the vote opens a phone player sees a chip reading VOTE LIVE and the heading of a card. The stage, the Drop button and every button are touch-action: none: a drag that starts on the canvas, the Drop button or the help text scrolled 0 px, while a drag from the header scrolled 225 px. In multiplayer the turn card is also mostly below the fold.
findings.repro: Play solo on a phone-sized viewport and wait 8 s.
findings.why_it_matters: The vote is the game's signature moment and the solo player's only agency over it. On the device most players will use, it is out of sight and hard to reach while a 3.5 s timer runs.
findings.suggested_change: Add a compact vote strip (three chips with icon, short name and count) pinned to the bottom edge of the stage whenever a vote is open, and show the active effect and its time left on the stage. Restrict touch-action: none to the canvas and Drop; use pan-y elsewhere.

findings.title: The Room button bounces straight back to the game, so nobody can leave or close a live room
findings.what_happens: During a live round the header button reads Room. Clicking it switches to the lobby and the next state update switches back: host game → lobby at 160 ms → game at 241 ms; player game → lobby at 163 ms → game at 440 ms. Close room, Leave room and Back to round are never reachable while a round is live. The lobby even carries the text 'The round is live. Use Back to round to return to play.'
findings.repro: Start any multiplayer round and click Room as host or player.
findings.why_it_matters: A host cannot stop a round that has gone wrong and a player cannot leave politely; the only exit is closing the tab, which in Competitive forfeits the stack (F-006). The cause, a snapshot handler that forces the game screen, is inferred from timing and not read line by line.
findings.suggested_change: Remember that the user chose the lobby view and do not switch screens on snapshots until they press Back to round or the phase changes.

findings.title: Competitive: a sub-second disconnect permanently ends your stack
findings.what_happens: A player's socket was closed at 36 s. The client showed 'Connection lost. Rejoining automatically…' and was back in under a second, to 'Your stack is finished. You can watch the room.' The results list them as Disconnected at height 17. In Teamwork the same event only forfeits the turn.
findings.repro: In a Competitive round, drop a player's connection for a moment (network handoff, locked screen, tab discarded).
findings.why_it_matters: Phones lose sockets constantly. One blip costs the whole 90 s round and teaches the player nothing.
findings.suggested_change: Give a grace window (for example 10 s) in which the stack is frozen, not ended; end it only if the player has not resumed by then.

findings.title: Competitive: every sabotage hits the leader; everyone else never experiences one
findings.what_happens: The winner of each vote is applied to the tallest connected stack only. In the test round 7 of 7 sabotages went to the leader and 0 to the other player, whose panel read 'Sabotage over' throughout. The vote cadence also follows the leader's height, so past height 25 the leader is under an effect about 5 s in every 7. Players are not shown who is being hit.
findings.repro: Play a Competitive round with one player clearly ahead.
findings.why_it_matters: With six players, five are playing a plain stacker while the headline feature happens to someone else, and the safest strategy is to sit just behind the leader. It is a strong catch-up tool, but it removes the game's fantasy for most of the room.
findings.suggested_change: Keep the leader bias but spread it: leader plus one random other stack, or everyone with the leader getting the full duration. Tell every player who is being sabotaged and with what. Validate with playtest experiment E5.

findings.title: Teamwork: play stops for every 5-second vote, players cannot vote, and the UI says the block keeps moving
findings.what_happens: Teamwork opens votes between turns and starts no turn until the vote resolves. For 5 s every player sees WAIT YOUR TURN, a 0 s timer, three disabled vote buttons and the text 'The block keeps moving. The host is choosing the room vote.' The control help still says 'Keep stacking during votes.' Only the host can vote in either mode.
findings.repro: Play Teamwork past 8 s and watch a player's screen.
findings.why_it_matters: Players already wait for each other's turns (one turn in six in a full room). Adding a 5 s freeze every 10 s in which they can do nothing, while the copy says otherwise, is the largest block of dead time in the game.
findings.suggested_change: Let players who are not on turn cast the room vote from their phones (the host's click can be one more vote or the tie-break), and fix the copy. This turns the dead time into the 'chat' the title promises.

findings.title: Teamwork: any sabotage can be waited out inside the 10-second turn at no cost
findings.what_happens: The effect clock starts when the turn starts. Timed effects last 5 s and drop-counted ones 8 s; the turn lasts 10 s and Teamwork has no round clock. Observed: Crumble expired at 7.5 s with the turn timer showing 2 s; a 5 s effect leaves 5 s. The effect card then reads 'Sabotage over' and the player drops clean.
findings.repro: In Teamwork, when you are sabotaged, wait until the effect timer ends, then drop.
findings.why_it_matters: A team that notices this never plays under sabotage, and the best strategy makes every turn slower for everyone watching.
findings.suggested_change: In Teamwork count effects in drops, not seconds: the effect lasts until the targeted player's block lands. Solo is already protected by its 3.5 s auto-drop.

findings.title: Teamwork: an idle or hidden teammate costs 12 s per rotation or drops a block at random, and nobody can skip or remove them
findings.what_happens: At 10 s the server requests an auto-drop and the client sends its current position. A visible idle tab therefore drops the block wherever it is, which on a narrow tower ends the round for everyone. A hidden tab (frame loop paused, socket alive) sends a stale position, is rejected with DROP_POSITION_OUT_OF_SYNC and forfeits 2 s later: 12 s per rotation, observed twice in a row, with the team placing one block in 30 s. There is no skip, kick or idle detection.
findings.repro: In Teamwork, have one player switch tabs or simply stop playing.
findings.why_it_matters: One distracted phone stalls or sinks the whole room, and the host has no tool except closing the room, which F-005 makes unreachable mid-round.
findings.suggested_change: On timeout, forfeit the turn without dropping. After a turn with no input, skip that player until they act. Give the host a skip control.

findings.title: Screen-reader users hear almost nothing during play, and in multiplayer a whole list is re-announced on every drop
findings.what_happens: A 17 s solo run offered three messages: one PERFECT (20 perfects landed; identical text is not re-set), the effect's name, and the collapse. Nothing when the vote opened, nothing for the options, nothing when the effect ended, no turn timer. Status text for those events is written to game.statusMessage in seven places and rendered only when it starts with 'Vote'. In multiplayer the aria-live player list rewrote itself 108 times in 75 s. No real screen reader was run: this is what the DOM offers to one.
findings.repro: Run a solo game with a MutationObserver on the aria-live regions, or with a screen reader.
findings.why_it_matters: Rated P1 on the brief's scale because a group is effectively shut out. Timing by ear is not possible today at all (see appendix A-04), so better announcements help low-vision screen-reader users first.
findings.suggested_change: Announce vote open with the three names, the winner with its one-line description, and effect end, through one polite region; clear the toast before re-setting it; take aria-live off the player lists and announce only turn changes ('Your turn', 'Ada's turn').

findings.title: Space always drops, so it cannot activate a focused vote option or the Menu button during play
findings.what_happens: With a vote option focused, Space dropped a block and cast no vote; Enter cast the vote. With Menu focused, Space dropped a block and stayed in the game.
findings.repro: During a vote, Tab to an option and press Space.
findings.why_it_matters: Keyboard users expect Space to press the focused button. Here it costs them a block.
findings.suggested_change: Let Space drop only when focus is on the body, the canvas or the Drop button.

findings.title: The vote card shows three names with no explanation, never marks your pick, and applies the ×4 weight silently
findings.what_happens: Options are an icon, a name and a count ('Spotlight', 'Crumble'). Descriptions exist but live in the How to play guide. After clicking an option its class, aria-pressed, border, background and the subtitle were unchanged; only the count rose. The player's choice is worth four votes at the tally, which makes it decisive (wins 77% among three harsh options, 19.5% when backing Superglue versus 8.6% unvoted) but the card never says which option is theirs.
findings.repro: Play solo, click an option at the first vote, move the pointer away.
findings.why_it_matters: For a first-timer the choice is blind and has 5 s; for everyone the strongest lever they hold gives no confirmation.
findings.suggested_change: Add a one-line effect per option (the strings already exist in the sabotage list), a selected state with aria-pressed and a 'Your pick ×4' tag, and keep 'Vote counted' on screen.

findings.title: Host voting: every click adds another vote and cannot be changed, while the help text says one choice per person
findings.what_happens: Three host clicks on one option produced counts of 3, 0, 0: each click is recorded as a new voter (manual-1, manual-2…). The card still shows the solo help: 'One choice per person; in Solo your choice carries four chat votes. Change it any time.'
findings.repro: Host a room, start a round, click one vote option several times.
findings.why_it_matters: The host alone decides every sabotage, which may be the intent for a streamer, but the rules on screen describe something else and a mis-click cannot be undone.
findings.suggested_change: Decide the model. Either one changeable host vote (use a fixed voter id), or say plainly 'Each click adds a chat vote'. Show mode-specific help.

findings.title: When the host leaves, players are not told; votes resolve at random and nobody can rematch
findings.what_happens: After the host's browser closed, the players' state carried hostConnected: false but nothing on screen changed. The next vote still read 'The host is choosing the room vote', closed with counts 0, 0, 0 and a random winner was applied. Rematch is host-only and there is no host migration, so after the round the room can only idle out (10 min). The rematch dead end is inferred from code.
findings.repro: Start a round and close the host tab.
findings.why_it_matters: The room looks alive but is leaderless, and it ends in a dead end.
findings.suggested_change: Show 'Host disconnected' to players. While the host is away, skip votes or let players vote. Let any player rematch after a short wait.

findings.title: Multiplayer needs a host plus two players on separate devices, and nothing says so before you host
findings.what_happens: The host is a non-playing stream view. With a host and one player, Start round stays disabled: 'Waiting for at least two connected players.' The title buttons say only 'Teamwork · Host a room'. How to play covers solo only; team score, turn order, the host role and Competitive rules are explained nowhere. This audit's own brief assumed two browsers would be enough.
findings.repro: Host Teamwork on one device and join from one other.
findings.why_it_matters: Two friends who want to play together cannot, and find out only in the lobby.
findings.suggested_change: Say it on the title ('Host on a big screen · 2-6 phones join'), add a multiplayer section to How to play, and consider letting the host also play, or a two-device mode.

findings.title: Reduced motion is honoured in the rules but never explained, and there is no in-game motion setting
findings.what_happens: With the OS preference set, the five excluded effects never appeared (4 solo ballots, 4 Teamwork ballots, 7 Competitive ballots after a mid-round change) and render static in the DEV lab. But no screen mentions it: the guide still says 'Meet all 16 active sabotages', and #motion-chip is a speed readout. One reduced-motion player silently reduces the pool for the whole room. Players without the OS setting cannot turn off Earthquake (whole scene, about 7-11 Hz, 5 s) or Pisa. The eight effects that stay are small-object motion or held view changes and looked acceptable; Slow-to-Dart's ×2.5 lunges and Macro Zoom's scale change are the two to test with motion-sensitive players.
findings.repro: Enable reduced motion in the OS and play; or join a room where another player has it enabled.
findings.why_it_matters: The protection works, which is a real strength, but players cannot see it, choose it, or understand why a room's ballots look different.
findings.suggested_change: Add a Motion control next to Theme (Full / Reduced, defaulting to the OS setting, stored like the theme). When reduced, say '11 of 16 sabotages active' in the guide and show a small 'Reduced motion room' tag in the lobby.

findings.title: The perfect window is a flat ±3 px that players cannot see; difficulty rises through speed alone
findings.what_happens: Every unaffected drop used a 3.00 px window. Because speed climbs from 140 to 300 px/s, the window in time shrinks from 42.9 ms to 20 ms by height 32 and then stays flat. The speed/120 term only ever applies under speed effects (Slow-to-Dart from height 1, Slingshot from 7, Drunk from 10, Turbo from 15; observed 3.40-3.75 under Turbo) and equals one 60 Hz frame of travel: a floor, not a curve. The effect-adjusted speed is passed correctly at every call site. Nothing on the stage marks the centre or the window before the drop.
findings.repro: Read the perfect-window value on each drop (data/matrix.json → drops).
findings.why_it_matters: It is coherent as designed, but a 20 ms invisible target is near chance for most people, and after height 32 nothing new is asked of the player.
findings.suggested_change: Keep the formula. Add a faint centre tick on the top block (at least for the first ten blocks), and consider a late-game ramp that is not speed. Test with experiment E1 before changing numbers.

findings.title: Effect set: four speed effects look like normal play, one helper is classed as harsh, two are near-neutral, and Spotlight hides almost everything
findings.what_happens: No two effects ever interact: one runs per target and a new one replaces it (0 of 120 pairs). In stills, Turbo, Drunk Block, Slow-to-Dart and Gravity Slingshot are identical to normal play apart from the label. Drafting Calipers keeps the block within 38 px of the tower, which makes a miss impossible above 38 px width, yet it is on the harsh list and simulated chat weights it ×3. Rollercoaster only bobs the block vertically; Portal Walls lands on the best-overlap wrap. Turbo and Slingshot do the same job, Slingshot harder. Spotlight leaves one small beam on a black field. The Shell Game's 'crack' is a few pixels. Counts are balanced (4 per category, each on 18-19% of ballots); harshness is not, and under reduced motion the pool is 4/1/3/3 with three helpers or neutrals in eleven. Seven of sixteen effects change only the view, so their value could not be judged by a bot.
findings.repro: Open the DEV lab and step through the sixteen effects.
findings.why_it_matters: Variety is the game's content. Effects that cannot be told apart, or that help while billed as harm, dilute it.
findings.suggested_change: Give each speed effect an on-stage look (streaks, wobble, wind-up, arcs). Move Calipers off the harsh list or invert it. Rework or cut Rollercoaster; merge Turbo and Slingshot. Widen Spotlight's beam at low heights and enlarge the Shell Game marker. Rank by experiment E3 first.

findings.title: Developer tooling is in the player's path: DEV lab on the title and in the live game header, 'BUILD 01' in the heading
findings.what_happens: 'DEV lab · Test all 16' is the third primary button on the title, and a DEV lab button sits beside Menu during every solo run, where a mis-tap leaves the run. The lab itself is a good practice space, but its panel copy is written for developers ('Offline test bench', 'fixture').
findings.repro: Open the title screen; start a solo game on a phone.
findings.why_it_matters: New players are offered a developer tool before they have played, and the one safe place to learn effects is mislabelled.
findings.suggested_change: Rename and reframe it as Practice ('Try any sabotage'), remove the in-run button, drop 'BUILD 01'.

findings.title: If the socket hangs, 'Connecting to the game server…' stays forever with no timeout, progress or way out
findings.what_happens: With /ws accepted but never answered, the title showed the same line at 0.3, 2, 5, 10 and 20 s; the header read 'Teamwork · reconnecting' on a first connection; the mode buttons stayed enabled and nothing is marked busy. The join dialog shows 'Connecting to the room…' the same way. Refusals are handled well (immediate message, solo still works) and a 7 s delay ends in the lobby; a mid-lobby outage retries with backoff and recovered 3 s after the server returned.
findings.repro: Block or stall /ws and press Host Teamwork.
findings.why_it_matters: On a free hosting plan the server sleeps. A player who clicks Host from a tab left open sees a static sentence for as long as the wake-up takes.
findings.suggested_change: After 5 s say 'Waking the server, this can take up to a minute'; after 30 s offer Retry and Play solo. Use 'connecting', not 'reconnecting', before the first connection. Replace 'Check the server' with player wording.

findings.title: Decision-critical text is 9-11 px on phones
findings.what_happens: Paper: vote option names 11 px, vote help and vote state 10 px, one label 9 px, the speed and effect chip 11 px, control help 11 px. Sunset sets Press Start 2P at 11 px for the effect name and strong text. Prime Time has 10 px labels. Contrast is fine; size is not, and there is no font-size setting.
findings.repro: Open the game screen at 360 or 390 px wide.
findings.why_it_matters: The smallest type carries the vote and the active effect, which must be read in seconds while playing.
findings.suggested_change: Set a 12 px floor for labels and 14 px for vote names and the effect name on phones; pixel fonts need 12 px or more.

findings.title: Every drop re-sends the whole room: room.state reached 30 KB with about 100 blocks
findings.what_happens: room.state carries every block of every stack and is broadcast on each change. Observed maximum 10.1 KB (Teamwork, height 36) and 30.3 KB (Competitive, two players, about 100 blocks); a player received 138 of them plus 1,005 position messages in a 62 s round. A code comment already cites about 52 KB per change for six players at height 40. Size grows with players × height while the drop rate grows with players.
findings.repro: Log message sizes during a long Competitive round.
findings.why_it_matters: On mobile data a full room costs megabytes per round and risks jank on slow phones. Not load-tested here; six-player figures are extrapolated.
findings.suggested_change: Send deltas for drops (block.land already exists) and reserve the full snapshot for join, resume and round start.

findings.title: Teamwork: 'up to 3 drops' effects cover one drop in practice, except Crumble
findings.what_happens: Portal Walls, Superglue and Calipers are targeted at the player whose turn it is and count only that player's drops. The next player is not affected, and the 8 s limit usually passes before the first player's turn returns. Crumble is team-global and does last three drops. How to play describes all four the same way.
findings.repro: Code path: effectApplies → consumeDropEffects, with turn rotation.
findings.why_it_matters: A Superglue 'bribe' that helps one drop is a weaker beat than the text promises.
findings.suggested_change: Make all four team-global in Teamwork, or reword to 'your next drop'.

findings.title: Peekaboo fades out, flashes back for 40 ms, then cuts to hidden
findings.what_happens: peekabooOpacity returns 1 until 0.31 s, fades to 0 by 0.35 s, then climbs back to 0.975 by 0.389 s and drops to 0 at 0.39 s. The in-game text says it 'fades over 40 ms, then stays hidden'. Frame sampling counted 3 blink pairs per second over 1.7% of the canvas: far below any flash threshold, but one more blink than intended.
findings.repro: Evaluate Core.peekabooOpacity at 0.33, 0.37, 0.385 and 0.39.
findings.why_it_matters: A stray ghost frame makes the effect harder to read fairly.
findings.suggested_change: Return 0 from 0.35 s to the end of the cycle.

findings.title: Copy and HUD drift: repeated speed in the chip, '+1 TEAM BONUS' in Competitive, 'Turn timer' on the round clock, and more
findings.what_happens: The chip reads 'VOTE LIVE · 230 PX/S · 230 PX/S' during votes and '170 PX/S · 170 PX/S' for non-targets. Competitive perfects toast 'PERFECT DROP · +1 TEAM BONUS'. The 90 s round clock is labelled 'Turn timer'. The turn heading reads 'the next player's turn' in lower case. Player rows say '1 blocks'. The host view keeps 'One press, one drop. Keep stacking during votes.' On the host board the chip covers the second player's name. Results say 'One tower survived the chaos' when none did. Toast and banner both say PERFECT at once.
findings.repro: See the listed screenshots.
findings.why_it_matters: Each is small; together they make the multiplayer modes read as less finished than solo.
findings.suggested_change: A copy pass per mode and role; print the speed once.

findings.title: The sound setting is forgotten on reload
findings.what_happens: Sound is off by default, which is the right default. Turning it on set aria-pressed and the label; after a reload it was off again and localStorage held nothing for it. Only the theme is stored.
findings.repro: Turn sound on, reload.
findings.why_it_matters: Players who want sound must turn it on every visit.
findings.suggested_change: Store the choice next to the theme; audio still starts only after a user gesture.

findings.title: axe: one contrast miss, no h1 outside the title screen, labels on role-less elements
findings.what_happens: Across 54 runs: #effect-label is 4.45:1 in Paper (11 px bold, needs 4.5). Lobby, game and results have no level-one heading because the only h1 is on the hidden title screen. aria-label sits on .brand, .mode-row and .height-chip, which have no role, so 'Blocks placed' may be ignored.
findings.repro: Run axe-core on the game screen in the Paper theme.
findings.why_it_matters: Minor, and cheap to clear.
findings.suggested_change: Darken the label one step; make each screen's main heading an h1 (or keep one visually hidden h1); give labelled containers role=group or use visible text.

findings.title: Vote adapter seam (not wired to a live source): no voter namespacing or caps, and it shares ids with the host's clicks
findings.what_happens: receiveChatVote hands the event to recordVote: one vote per trimmed voterId, last write wins (so changing a vote is allowed and duplicates collapse). There is no length limit (a 100,000-character id was accepted), no platform prefix, no rate limit, and the id space is shared with manual-N host votes, so a chat user called manual-1 would overwrite a host click. Host clicks are unlimited while each chat voter has one vote.
findings.repro: Call Core.recordVote with the ids described.
findings.why_it_matters: Nothing today, since no chat source is connected. It matters the day Twitch or YouTube is plugged in.
findings.suggested_change: When wiring a source: prefix ids by platform, cap id length and distinct voters per ballot, keep host votes in a separate bucket, and take ids from the platform's authenticated payload only.

findings.title: package.json allows Node 20, but the tests need Node 22.22.2 or newer and fail misleadingly on 20
findings.what_happens: On Node 20.20.2 npm test reported 30 tests, 29 passing and 1 failing (earthquake.test.js), and four suites skipped with 'jsdom / @napi-rs/canvas not installed (run npm install)'. Both are installed; jsdom 30.1.3 requires Node ^22.22.2 and throws on load. On Node 22.23.4 the result is 42 of 42, matching the brief. The server itself runs fine on Node 20.
findings.repro: Run npm ci && npm test on Node 20.
findings.why_it_matters: A contributor on a supported-looking Node sees a red suite and a wrong hint. No player impact.
findings.suggested_change: Set engines to the real minimum (or pin an older jsdom), add .nvmrc, and make the skip message report the actual error.

appendix.title: Clients keep sending player.position after a round ends or their stack ends, drawing 29 error replies per round (ROUND_NOT_LIVE, PLAYER_INACTIVE).
Multiplayer results leave focus on <body>; solo moves it to Play again.
Room codes are four letters from 24 (331,776); join attempts are limited only by the per-socket rate limit and there is no kick, so a stranger could reach an open lobby. Note-only; not tested.
No non-visual way to play: sound is off by default and no cue encodes the mover's position. Idea: an optional pitch sweep for position.
Player colours 2 and 4 (teal #2F8478, vermilion #D5472F) have nearly equal luminance; a likely red-green confusion pair where no name is adjacent.
Macro Zoom draws blocks over the bottom hint; the chat flavour pop overlaps the tower.
In Sunset the speed and effect chip wraps to two lines and covers more of the stage.
#theme-select keeps the browser's default focus ring instead of the themed one.
Late joiners get a clear 'This room has already started.' but no way to watch. Idea: spectator join.
The context menu is disabled on every button, which also removes long-press actions for assistive tools.
The Competitive host board is about 405 px wide inside an 870 px panel: small for a screen meant to be streamed.
The disabled Start round button is 2.48:1 in Sunset: exempt from contrast rules, but hard to read as a button at all.
There is no pause in solo other than hiding the tab.
